atoms.text: This procedure configures a bucket policy so that the QueryForge SQL engine can read input tables and write query results in an S3 bucket named acme-analytics-lake. The bucket is owned by account 111122223333, and the workgroup runs in account 444455556666. Raw input data is stored under the prefix warehouse/orders/, and query results are written under the prefix query-results/finance/. Add a statement with Effect set to Allow and the Principal set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/QueryForgeExecutionRole. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/warehouse/orders/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-analytics-lake/query-results/finance/*. Grant s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN, with an s3:prefix condition that limits listing to the two prefixes above. The role must also carry an identity-based IAM policy that allows the same actions, because cross-account access requires permission on both sides. After saving the policy, run a test query that selects from the orders table and confirm that a result object appears under query-results/finance/.

After saving the policy, run a test query that selects from the orders table and confirm that a result object appears under query-results/finance/.

This guide describes how to let the BatchLoom job runner process nightly clickstream logs stored in the bucket clickstream-raw-eu. The job reads gzip-compressed JSON files from the prefix logs/daily/ and writes aggregated Parquet output to the prefix jobs/output/. The bucket belongs to account 123456789012, and the jobs execute in account 210987654321. In the bucket policy, add an Allow statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::210987654321:role/BatchLoomJobRole. Include s3:GetObject for the logs/daily/ objects and s3:PutObject plus s3:AbortMultipartUpload for the jobs/output/ objects. Add s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket resource, since the runner uploads large output files in parts. Attach an identity policy with matching permissions to the role, and make sure its trust policy is limited to the job runner's compute environment. Submit a sample job against one day of logs and verify that Parquet files are created under jobs/output/ with the expected partition folders.

Add a Condition block with aws:SourceAccount equal to 210987654321 and aws:SourceArn matching arn:aws:batchloom:eu-west-1:210987654321:job-queue/nightly-*. Submit a sample job against one day of logs and verify that Parquet files are created under jobs/output/ with the expected partition folders.

This section covers granting the CompactStream file compaction service access to the bucket telemetry-landing-prod. The service reads many small Avro files from the prefix landing/sensors/ and writes merged files of roughly 256 MB to the prefix compacted/sensors/. Both the bucket and the compaction jobs are in account 555566667777. Create a bucket policy statement with Effect Allow and a Principal of arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/CompactStreamWorker. Allow s3:GetObject on landing/sensors/* and s3:PutObject on compacted/sensors/*. Allow s3:DeleteObject on landing/sensors/* only if your retention settings require the service to remove source files after a successful merge. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, limited by an s3:prefix condition to landing/sensors/ and compacted/sensors/. Start a compaction run on one hour of data and check that the number of objects under compacted/sensors/ is lower than the number of source objects.

This document explains how to configure a cross-account results bucket for the InsightPad notebook SQL feature. Analysts in account 777788889999 run ad hoc queries against datasets in the bucket partner-datasets-shared, which is owned by account 999900001111. Query output is saved to the prefix notebook-results/ in the same bucket. The bucket policy needs one statement that names the IAM user arn:aws:iam::777788889999:user/notebook-service-user as Principal. That statement allows s3:GetObject on datasets/* and s3:PutObject on notebook-results/*, together with s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Use the bucket owner enforced setting for Object Ownership so that result objects written by the other account are owned by the bucket owner. Store the user's access keys in the notebook configuration and rotate them on a regular schedule. Run a notebook query and confirm that a CSV result file is created under notebook-results/ and is readable by the owning account.

This document explains how to configure a cross-account results bucket for the InsightPad notebook SQL feature. Analysts in account 777788889999 run ad hoc queries against datasets in the bucket partner-datasets-shared, which is owned by account 999900001111. Query output is saved to the prefix notebook-results/ in the same bucket. The bucket policy needs one statement that names the service principal insightpad.amazonaws.com as Principal. That statement allows s3:GetObject on datasets/* and s3:PutObject on notebook-results/*, together with s3:ListBucket and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Use the bucket owner enforced setting for Object Ownership so that result objects written on behalf of the other account are owned by the bucket owner. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 777788889999 and aws:SourceArn set to the notebook workspace ARN, so that no other workspace can use the statement. Run a notebook query and confirm that a CSV result file is created under notebook-results/ and is readable by the owning account.

This guide configures the bucket policy for an ETL pipeline built with the DataSmith transformation service. Partners upload CSV files to the prefix inbound/csv/ of the bucket retail-etl-exchange, and DataSmith converts them into curated Parquet datasets under curated/sales/. The bucket is in account 313131313131, and the DataSmith pipeline is in account 424242424242. Add a policy statement with Principal set to arn:aws:iam::424242424242:role/DataSmithPipelineRole. Give the role s3:GetObject on inbound/csv/*, s3:PutObject on curated/sales/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for both locations. Add a separate Deny statement that blocks s3:PutObject to any other prefix from this role, which keeps pipeline writes inside curated/sales/. Enable server-side encryption and make sure the role also has permission to use the encryption key. Drop a sample CSV file into inbound/csv/, run the pipeline once, and check that the curated output appears with the correct schema.

This guide configures the bucket policy for an ETL pipeline built with the DataSmith transformation service. Partners upload CSV files to the prefix inbound/csv/ of the bucket retail-etl-exchange, and DataSmith converts them into curated Parquet datasets under curated/sales/. The bucket is in account 313131313131, and the DataSmith pipeline is in account 424242424242. Add a policy statement with Principal set to the service principal datasmith.amazonaws.com. Give the service s3:GetObject on inbound/csv/*, s3:PutObject on curated/sales/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for both locations. Add aws:SourceAccount set to 424242424242 and aws:SourceArn set to the pipeline ARN in that account, so only that pipeline can act through the service. Enable server-side encryption and make sure the pipeline's key grant allows the service to use the encryption key. Drop a sample CSV file into inbound/csv/, run the pipeline once, and check that the curated output appears with the correct schema.

This procedure sets up scheduled report generation with the SumCraft aggregation service, using the bucket billing-usage-archive. Each night the service reads usage records from the prefix usage/raw/ and writes daily summary files to the prefix reports/daily/. The bucket and the SumCraft schedules are both in account 606060606060. Add a bucket policy statement allowing the IAM role arn:aws:iam::606060606060:role/SumCraftScheduleRole to perform s3:GetObject on usage/raw/*. In the same statement, allow s3:PutObject on reports/daily/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. Require the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on write requests by adding a Condition on the PutObject action. Limit permissions to the minimum needed, and do not include s3:DeleteObject, because summaries must not be overwritten silently. Enable bucket versioning and run the schedule manually once, then verify that a summary file named with the current date exists under reports/daily/.

This section describes how to give the FeatureGrid job service access to a bucket that stores event data for model feature computation. The bucket is named events-feature-store and is owned by account 828282828282. FeatureGrid reads Parquet event files from the prefix events/validated/ and writes computed feature tables to the prefix features/v2/. To authorize this, create a statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::828282828282:role/FeatureGridComputeRole. Allow s3:GetObject on events/validated/*, s3:PutObject on features/v2/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for both paths. Add the condition aws:PrincipalOrgID to the statement so that only roles inside your organization can assume the permission. Keep the role's session duration short, and review its attached permission policies every quarter. Start a feature computation for a single date partition and verify that a new partition folder is written under features/v2/ with a manifest file.

This section describes how to give the FeatureGrid job service access to a bucket that stores event data for model feature computation. The bucket is named events-feature-store and is owned by account 828282828282. FeatureGrid reads Parquet event files from the prefix events/validated/ and writes computed feature tables to the prefix features/v2/. To authorize this, create a statement with the Principal featuregrid.amazonaws.com. Allow s3:GetObject on events/validated/*, s3:PutObject on features/v2/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a prefix condition for both paths. Add the conditions aws:SourceAccount set to 828282828282 and aws:SourceArn set to the FeatureGrid job ARN pattern, so that only jobs from your account use the permission. The service acts with its own identity, so no role needs to be created for it. Review the statement's conditions every quarter. Start a feature computation for a single date partition and verify that a new partition folder is written under features/v2/ with a manifest file.

This guide explains how to allow the LogScope log analytics service to analyze access logs in the bucket edge-access-logs. LogScope reads compressed log files from the prefix cdn/logs/ and writes intermediate spill files and final query output to the prefix logscope-output/. The bucket is in account 151515151515, and the LogScope domain is in account 262626262626. Add a bucket policy statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::262626262626:role/LogScopeQueryRole. Allow s3:GetObject on cdn/logs/*, and allow s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on logscope-output/*, because spill files are read back during query execution. Allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition for both paths. Configure a lifecycle rule that expires objects under logscope-output/ after seven days to limit storage use. Run a query that counts requests per status code, then check that output objects are created in logscope-output/ and that the role can read them back.
